StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterDeath.issue: The guards are exact -- `target != base.Owner && target.Side == base.Owner.Side && !base.Owner.IsDead` (RavenousPower.cs:26) maps line-for-line to powers.py:1594-1599 -- and the effect order matches (stun the owner, then grant Strength). Two divergences. (1) MISSING `applier=` on the Strength grant: RavenousPower.cs:33 passes `base.Owner` and powers.py:1602 omits it; same shape and same dormancy as power/high_voltage's, carried as its own guard below. (2) The `((CorpseSlug)base.Owner.Monster).IsRavenous` flag (RavenousPower.cs:31, cleared in StunnedMove at :41) has no sim counterpart at all -- the sim stuns and buffs but never marks the Corpse Slug as devouring. Whether that is observable depends on what reads IsRavenous on the monster; it is the Corpse Slug's own record to settle, and it is flagged here rather than waived because a monster-state flag set and cleared across a stun is the kind of thing an intent or a move branch reads. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.issue: MISSING `applier=`. C# passes `base.Owner` (`PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>(choiceContext, base.Owner, ..., base.Owner, null)`); the sim omits it, so `applier` is None through hooks.modify_power_amount (cmds.py:297), hooks.on_power_applied (cmds.py:327) and hooks.on_power_amount_changed (cmds.py:312), and the granted power's .applier is left None (powers.py:59). Recurring gap shape 5. DORMANT, executed: the sim's applier readers are RitualPower.__init__ (powers.py:195), _PossessPower._track (powers.py:3092-3099 -- needs `applier is self.owner` AND a player target AND a negative delta), UnsettlingLamp (relics/unsettling_lamp.py:47 -- needs `applier is self.player`) and the `creature is self.applier` on_death tests of shrink/constrict/dampen/hex; none matches an enemy self-buff with a positive delta. Reproduce with `py tools/audit/power_slot_probes.py applier-readers`. Same verdict as power/high_voltage's and power/territorial's (rule 3). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:1601 `CreatureCmd.stun(self.hooks, self.owner)`. Unlike FlutterPower's stun (which passes a next-state id and is a live RNG gap -- see audits/power/flutter.json), this one passes only the stunned move, so there is no move re-roll and no RNG stream to get wrong. Worth contrasting: the two stuns in half B look alike and only one is broken.
